title: Hole a 2 m sidehill putt in one stroke with a blade putter, on a green that falls 2 degrees across the line
instruction: Hole the golf ball with one stroke of the putter.
context: Putting is the part of golf everyone plays, on a course, a practice green or a mini-golf hole. Across a slope the ball curves downhill as it slows, so it must start well above the hole at just the right pace: too firm and it lips out or runs past, too soft and it falls away below the hole.
setup: Putting green: 3.05 x 0.61 m platform (38 x 89 mm pine rails on edge, 18 mm plywood, 10 mm putting turf), 11.7 cm high, running along x from x=8 cm on the robot table onto a second table of the same height (2.30 x 1.20 m top, centre x=2.07 m, y=35 cm). Its low long edge is at y=5 cm; the other rail sits on a 21 mm shim strip, so the turf falls 2.0 degrees towards -y. Hole: 108 mm across, white plastic cup 102 mm deep, centre at x=2.44 m, y=35 cm. Golf ball (42.7 mm, 45.9 g) on the turf at x=44 cm, y=35 cm, 2.00 m from the hole centre along x. Putter: right-handed blade, 35 in (0.89 m), 70-degree lie, steel head 105 x 25 x 24 mm (350 g), 10 mm steel shaft (120 g), 27 mm rubber grip 267 mm long (65 g); it lies face down on the green beside the ball, shaft along x, head towards the arms, shaft centre 14 cm up from the heel at x=34 cm, y=20.5 cm. Distractors on the robot table: ceramic mug 0.32 kg at (62, -30) cm; paper cup 12 g at (78, -12) cm; folded microfibre towel 20 x 21 cm, 60 g, at (45, -52) cm. Coordinates from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left; the robot table top is the reference height.
scoring: Fouls score 0 for the rest of the trial: the ball touched by a gripper (any finger point within 12 mm of its surface), or the putter touching the ball again once the ball is more than 30 cm from its spot (a second stroke). Otherwise: 1.0 if the ball rests in the hole (the whole ball below the turf surface, its centre within 54 mm of the hole's axis), moving under 5 mm/s, for at least 1 s, with every finger point at least 5 cm from it; 0.5 if it rests on the green (on the turf, under 5 mm/s) with its centre within 30 cm of the hole's centre; 0.25 if within 60 cm; 0 in every other case, including no stroke, a ball still rolling, or a ball off the green.
reset_notes: Put the ball back on its spot (a pencil dot on the turf) and lay the putter face down beside it on its tape marks. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid platform, turf and cup from convex pieces (24-sided hole, 54 mm apothem). Turf rolling resistance is an applied force, 0.0785 x the ball's weight against its rolling (stimp 10 ft), which also holds a stopped ball on the slope; no grain or grass texture. The ball is NVIDIA SimReady's golf ball colliding as an exact sphere; ball-face restitution 0.75. The putter (no SimReady putter exists), platform, cup and second table are primitives; the 3-degree loft is omitted. No force sensing.
